NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions expand history access, while residual connections support deeper networks. Diagnose the actual convolution graph: receptive-field span is 1 + Σ(kernel_width−1)×dilation for stride-one layers; enumerate reachable offsets to detect holes. Architectural access does not establish learned use: effective-receptive-field research shows influence can occupy only part of the theoretical field, although its findings concern vision CNNs rather than NextItNet. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), [effective receptive fields](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04128).

Activation-patching research provides transferable methodology, not established NextItNet-specific results. Zhang–Nanda’s ICLR 2024 study shows corruption choices and evaluation metrics can change localization conclusions; Heimersheim–Nanda (2024) explains interpretation pitfalls. For one frozen category network, compare matched histories differing only in a distant prefix or recent suffix; restore clean activations at selected positions and residual branches, and perform reverse ablations. Measure candidate-score margins alongside the fixed validation HR@10; test individual and grouped blocks because isolated interventions can miss distributed computation. [Patching best practices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042), [interpretation guide](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255).

Proposed controls, extrapolated from these sources: verify identity patches preserve outputs; use synthetic known-dependency inputs with a deterministic positive-control network; preserve sequence length, left padding and final-nonpadding readout during matched substitutions. Distinguish graph-inaccessible history from accessible history with little measured influence, without interpreting null effects as proof of irrelevance. Strong suffix sensitivity plus weak prefix sensitivity supports recent-item reliance only on the tested examples. Attribute a failure to dilation or a residual branch only after checking intervention artifacts and recovery across multiple matched pairs.
